key_inputs: Final runoff polls, latest per pollster with fieldwork ending 20-24 Oct: 18 pollsters, sample-weighted Flávio two-way share 50.79
Datafolha, Quaest and AtlasIntel final polls (23-24 Oct, 23-24 Oct, 18-23 Oct): mean 50.61
Runoff poll bias 2014/2018/2022 against the non-PT finalist: largest pollsters -0.86, -1.10, -1.86 (mean -1.27); all final polls -0.54, +1.46, -0.51 (mean +0.14)
First round 4 Oct 2026 (TSE): Flávio 47.03, Lula 45.16 of valid votes (two-way 51.01); final first-round polls underestimated Flávio's two-way share by 2.15 on average (2.38 for the three largest)
Turnout 2026 first round 78.92 %; first round to runoff change 2010 -3.38, 2014 -1.71, 2018 -0.97, 2022 +0.36; the 2022 change is carried over
Blank+null 2026 first round 4.77 % of votes cast; change 2018 +0.78, 2022 +0.18

sources.used_for: 2026 first-round electorate, turnout, blank and null votes
table of registered runoff and first-round polls (revision of 25 Oct 06:06 UTC, before polls opened); each poll's own link is in data/clean/polls_runoff_2026.csv
Datafolha final poll, 23-24 Oct, n=4,050, BR-09540/2026
Quaest final poll, 23-24 Oct, n=3,702, BR-09158/2026

notes: Poll-based: the final registered polls put Flávio at about 50.6-50.9 % of valid votes; in the 2014, 2018 and 2022 runoffs the largest pollsters underestimated the non-PT finalist by about 1.3 points, and in the 4 Oct first round every major pollster underestimated Flávio, so the estimate is moved toward him. The 80 % range and win probability assume an error SD of 1.5 points on the two-way share. Turnout is the 2026 first round plus the 2022 round-to-round change; blank/null adds the mean 2018/2022 change. Betting markets were not used.
